correctness.rationale: Condition on each specified H-component vertex set A: all crossing edges are absent, exterior Bernoulli(p) graph is independent, inside H contributes t_F(H), and connected F cannot straddle A. Subtract unconditional motif expectation and sum indicators to derive exact Cov(C_H,X_F)=E[C_H](t_F(H)-Q_F p^e(1-p)^s), with E[C_H]>0 and Q_F>0. The p-factor is monotone if s=0 and strictly unimodal if s>0; all endpoints t=0, t=Q and r=M are treated. For P3 inside an h-tree t=W=sum_v C(d_v,2); degree-excess transfer gives sharp unique path/star extremes, and the n>=h+1 induced ratio lies below 4/27. Independent complete rational G(n,p) enumerations reproduce eight mixed component/motif examples for n=4,5, both induced and noninduced. This is a universal conditional-expectation proof, not a deduction from those eight tests.
residual_risks: Model requires independent Bernoulli edges and connected motif F; covariance zero is not stochastic independence.

value.rationale: Connected-component type versus motif occurrence are natural random-graph observables; the exact sign of their dependence matters for motif-based inference. The full all-connected H,F identity gives a reusable component Palm law, while induced motifs exhibit a genuinely different two-transition regime, and paths/stars are uniquely extremal tree shapes. These exact structural boundaries are more than a normalization check, although the conditional expectation technique is elementary.
